messages:
Pranav: quick question — for sharded safetensors loading, should we bias hotcache warmups toward small high-use shards or big merged shards? thinking about tail latency and OOM risk
Liz: small-first seems safer for tail latency because they unblock many prefix ops quickly
Tim: agree, but small-first can thrash if we have lots of concurrent models that touch different small shards :/
Mike: tradeoff: small-first reduces p99 for short sequences, big-first improves throughput for long sequences where contiguous layers matter
Anna: another angle: prefer optimistic eager-read for shards with active leases, and lazy for everything else
Pranav: that lease idea — can we encode it in the loader API as prefetch_hint + lease_id? e.g. prefetch_hint: {priority: 10, lease: "req-1234"}
Liz: yes, expose prefetch_hint and a TTL. loader returns a handle with states: pending, ready, failed. runtime can attach backpressure
Tim: sketch of API:```json
{
  "shard_id": "m-0000-0001",
  "prefetch_hint": {"priority": 5, "lease": "l-42", "expected_ttl_s": 60},
  "mode": "optimistic" // optimistic | lazy | index-first
}
```
Mike: mode=index-first fallback is important for gzipped or remote bundles where streaming isn't possible
Pranav: implementation concerns: optimistic eager-read + big-shard-first could blow memory if too many long requests hit at once
Anna: so we need an admission controller that caps concurrent eager reads per-GPU and tracks estimated resident size per-shard
Liz: also add a soft quota with eviction hint: shards loaded via eager-read get an eviction_score boost for a window, then decay
Tim: scoring algo: score = usage_count * priority / (1 + time_since_last_access_s/half_life)
Mike: and factor in resident_size_bytes to avoid loading huge shards even if priority high
Pranav: I like the lease-based warmup to avoid wasted IO for speculative prefetching. If lease expires cancel IO and decrement priority
Anna: ops-bot can emit events on lease-grant and lease-revoke. e.g., "lease l-42 granted for req-1234"
ops-bot: (automated) lease l-42 granted -> node gpu-07, ttl 45s :white_check_mark:
Liz: metrics to track: prefetch_hit_rate, prefetch_cancel_rate, eager_io_bytes, eager_io_failures, eviction_reloads
Tim: and a debug trace per request: which shards requested, time to ready, whether fallback used (mmap/stream/index-first)
Mike: fallback strategies: stream-first for remote, mmap-first for local fast disk, index-first for manifest-less bundles. Always prefer zero-copy if available
Pranav: long-term refactor thought: move warmup policy from loader coordinator into runtime's scheduler to let it see cross-tenant signals (global mem pressure, network congestion)
Liz: yeah, but keep loader API stable: warmup hints in, state & telemetry out. runtime scheduler can read hints and global metrics to decide order
Anna: potential race: two requests both lease and try to hot-swap a shard; need an atomic handoff on the resident registry with compare-and-swap
Tim: atomic handoff pseudo:
```
if registry.claim(shard, expected_owner=null, new_owner=lease) {
  async load shard -> mark ready
} else {
  attach to existing load future
}
```
Mike: add a fallback attach pattern so later waiters attach to in-flight IO rather than duplicating it
Pranav: okay next action items: 1) add prefetch_hint fields to loader API (Liz), 2) prototype admission controller with resident_size accounting (Anna), 3) instrument ops-bot to emit lease events + telemetry (Mike), 4) doc an example scoring heuristic and edge cases (Tim)
Liz: +1. I'll PR the loader API JSON schema and a short example flow
Anna: I'll start a small sim for admission controller to tune thresholds
Mike: I'll wire ops-bot events to the telemetry pipeline; send sample event format in thread
Tim: I'll write the scoring doc and a couple of replayable scenarios for p99 vs throughput tradeoffs
Pranav: thanks all. keeping this thread as the coordination point. if we decide a different default for small-vs-big warmup, call it out in the PRs :thumbsup:
ops-bot: (automated) linked issue #2345 created: "warmup: prefetch hints + admission controller"
Pranav: perfect. filing follow-up: can we add a short test that asserts join-on-inflight-io to avoid duplicate reads?
